column1: # coverage-floors.tsv — the committed floors scripts/check-coverage.sh enforces
# (TST8). Three whitespace-separated columns:
#   <area>   a label, printed in the report
#   <regex>  a POSIX ERE matched against the profile's import path
#            (`srr/db_pack.go`, `srr/store/s3.go`) — the line:col span is
#            stripped before matching, so patterns are plain path regexes
#   <floor>  the minimum statement coverage percentage for that area
# Areas may overlap: `db` is also counted inside `total`. An area whose regex
# matches NOTHING fails loudly — a renamed file must not silently retire its
# own floor.
# THE MARGIN. Every floor is the LOWEST value measured across three runs of the
# tree that introduced it, truncated to a whole percent and then dropped one
# more point — so the slack is between 1.0 and 2.0 points depending on where the
# measurement fell. Chosen against three things. Two are honest ways a change
# moves the number down: adding an uncovered error branch to a hot file, and
# DELETING well-covered code (which raises the untested remainder's share of a
# smaller denominator). The third is measured, not hypothetical — the suite is
# not coverage-deterministic, which is why the floors were set off three runs
# and not one: `db` came in at 84.8 / 84.6 / 84.8 and `ingest` at 89.1 / 90.1 /
# 89.1, so part of the slack is simply the suite disagreeing with itself. (The
# statement COUNTS are stable — check-coverage.sh deduplicates blocks, see its
# header; before it did, the counts tripled depending on the build cache.) Much
# more slack and it stops being a ratchet; much less and every refactor becomes
# a floors edit, which trains people to lower them reflexively — the failure
# mode that kills coverage gates.
# Ratcheting up is a one-line diff here, and that is the point: when a batch of
# tests lands, truncate the new measurement and commit it.
# The areas are the risk surface, not the package list: `db` and `seen` are the
# store's byte-level writers (a regression there corrupts immutable objects
# under names cached forever), `store` the four backends behind them.
# The trailing comment on each row is the LOWEST of the three measurements the
# floor was derived from, on ce6825d (2026-07-26) — EXCEPT where the row says
# otherwise. A row carrying its own re-derivation note supersedes this line for
# that row alone; silently refreshing one number in place would leave this line
# lying about every other one.
# STORE, re-derived at HEAD (2026-07-26). The store tests in this push took the
# area 80.4 -> 85.8, which left the 79.0 floor 6.8 points low — gating none of
# them, and none of the next regression either. Ratcheted to 84.0: 1.8 points of
# slack, the TOP of the 1.0-2.0 band rather than the middle, because this is ONE
# measurement and not the three the other rows rest on. A single sample cannot
# see the ~1-point run-to-run spread the note above records, and more backend
# tests were landing alongside this edit. Those can only push the number UP
# (coverage rises when tests are added, and _test.go files are not instrumented
# into the profile), so what the extra slack pads against is the suite
# disagreeing with itself, not the concurrent work. Confirmed immediately after:
# the run that verified this edit read 87.8, i.e. 3.8 of slack — but its store
# suite was RED (an sftp redial test still landing), so that sample is not a
# derivation. Re-derive on a green tree and this row has a second point to give.
# area      pattern                  floor    measured
total       .                         84.0  # 85.1  every package in the profile
db          ^srr/db[^/]*\.go$         83.0  # 84.6  the pack/meta/expire/out writers
seen        ^srr/seen\.go$            88.0  # 89.7  the dedup sidecar's binary codec
store       ^srr/store/               84.0  # 85.8  the four storage backends (STORE, above)
mod         ^srr/mod/                 94.0  # 95.7  the content pipeline
ingest      ^srr/ingest/              88.0  # 89.1  the feed parser + external protocol
